expectations.text: States that source order in `nuget.config` is ignored during restore, so any listed source can serve any ID
expectations.evidence: NuGet ignores source order during restore

expectations.text: Adds a `<packageSourceMapping>` block mapping `Pellucid.*` to the Azure Artifacts source and `*` to nuget.org
States the most specific pattern wins, so `Pellucid.*` beats `*`
Adds `<clear />` under `<packageSources>` to stop machine-level sources leaking in
Rewrites the credential as `%FEED_TOKEN%`, stating `%VAR%` syntax works on every OS and `$VAR` never resolves, which explains the Linux 401s
Keeps the credential value an environment variable injected from the secret store, never a literal in the committed file
Warns that a package already in the global packages folder skips mapping and prescribes a per-repo `globalPackagesFolder` in CI
Warns that metadata commands (`dotnet package add`, `dotnet list package --outdated`) still query every source
expectations.evidence: dotnet list package --outdated still query every source

expectations.text: Prescribes committing lock files (`RestorePackagesWithLockFile`) and restoring with `--locked-mode` in CI
Recommends reserving the `Pellucid.` ID prefix on nuget.org as the publisher-side defense against the public 9.0.0

Prescribes a probe querying the internal endpoint's metadata for the public `Pellucid.Core.Common` name and asserting an exact not-found status, after a positive control on a real internal package, treating 401/403/5xx as inconclusive
expectations.evidence: Step 3 greps for "9.0.0" rather than asserting exact 404

expectations.text: Checks that `packages.lock.json` records the internal source for every `Pellucid.*` entry
expectations.evidence: every Pellucid.Core.* entry must point at the Azure Artifacts source

expectations.text: Uses a read-only feed credential for CI, separate from any publish identity
expectations.evidence: read-only PAT, separate from any publish identity
